profile.campus: AWS Oregon (US-WEST-2) -- Boardman / Umatilla / Hermiston campus, Morrow & Umatilla counties
profile.address: 79388, Olson Road Southeast, Boardman, Morrow County, Oregon, 97818
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures Amazon Web Services operates in Morrow and Umatilla counties in eastern Oregon, near the towns of Boardman, Umatilla, and Hermiston along the Columbia River. This is among AWS's original hyperscale campus locations, chosen for proximity to relatively low cost hydroelectric power generated along the Columbia River system, and it has expanded substantially since AWS's first Oregon buildings went up in the early 2010s.

Amazon's own aboutamazon.com materials on the region's economic impact state that AWS invested $15.6 billion in Morrow and Umatilla counties between 2012 and 2021, contributing $1.1 billion to local gross domestic product, and that AWS supported more than 1,800 full time direct employees across the two counties along with thousands of additional local jobs in construction, facilities maintenance, and electricity generation. Amazon states its Oregon data centers pay the highest local tax contributions in both counties, that it recycles roughly 96 percent of its cooling water back to local farmers at no charge, and that it draws at least 95 percent of the electricity powering the campus from renewable sources. Oregon Public Broadcasting and DataCenterDynamics have reported on AWS's continued expansion in Hermiston and Morrow County since 2025, including additional land acquisitions and plans local coverage ties to AI-focused, large scale data center construction, alongside continuing state and local tax abatements under Oregon's strategic investment program.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating for this individual building, and no source found for this page breaks the Morrow/Umatilla County AWS campus down building by building. This structure is treated as part of the documented AWS Oregon footprint described above.

profile.regional_context: Morrow and Umatilla counties in eastern Oregon form one of AWS's oldest and largest hyperscale data center regions, drawn originally by inexpensive hydroelectric power from Columbia River dams operated by the Bonneville Power Administration and delivered locally through the Umatilla Electric Cooperative. Oregon's strategic investment program lets counties offer long term property tax abatements to large capital projects in exchange for community service fee payments, an incentive structure Morrow and Umatilla counties have used repeatedly to attract AWS and other data center operators. Water rights and cooling water use have become a recurring local policy issue as the campus has expanded, covered by Oregon Public Broadcasting and regional outlets. The Boardman-Hermiston corridor is also drawing interest from other data center developers citing the same power and land availability that first attracted AWS, per Data Center Frontier reporting on competing projects in the area.

reading.body:
AWS does not publish specific power capacity, square footage, or technical specifications for individual data center buildings as a matter of stated security policy. This building is one facility within AWS's Boardman-area campus in Morrow County, Oregon, but its own capacity cannot be confirmed from AWS-owned sources. Industry tracking aggregators report an 80 MW figure for the broader campus and describe a multi-billion-dollar exascale AI expansion in the region, but these figures come from trade press and data center trackers rather than AWS publications and remain unconfirmed.

The Boardman campus sits on the Columbia River in eastern Oregon, chosen originally for access to hydroelectric power. AWS has announced plans for at least four additional data centers in Morrow County and local and trade press describe an active, large-scale expansion focused on AI workloads. Without published per-facility specifications, this individual building's role in that expansion cannot be quantified, but the campus context indicates material AI infrastructure investment in the region.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 publish power capacity. The state's published total is 156.6 MW across those eight facilities. AWS Boardman ranks ninth by published MW in Oregon, but this ranking reflects the absence of published specifications from AWS rather than a measure of actual capacity. The campus matters to AI scaling primarily as part of a documented hyperscale expansion, not as a specified facility.
